mathAssessment.frozenFamily: The accepted104 14/9-atom program, both source-defined routes, actual finite slot0 S and full current H1 are reconstructed from authenticated own H0 and packets. The two fixed-prefix rows are copied. Only the second-slot routing constraint is relaxed.
mathAssessment.finiteLaw: For each row and one of nine frozen FP32 atoms: binary64 addition, FP32 RNE, BF16 RNE, retaining the finite BF16 state exactly in FP32/FP64 carriers. The reused finite helper rejects nonfinite input/intermediate/post-round values.
mathAssessment.objective: Each disjoint pair uses separately formed (Cj-Ci)-(Yj-Yi), not the relaxed fitting target P*(Y-S). Endpoint and response measures are separately normalized; discovery uses retained104 energies plus diagnostic recomputation, transfer computes its analogous own reference energies. Zero energy retains the absolute weighted term.
mathAssessment.enumeration: All 81 ordered pair choices and nine singleton choices are evaluated. No node appears in two pairs; each component therefore admits an independent minimum. C-order a-major/b-minor argmin and smallest-index exact ties are explicit.
mathAssessment.exactnessBoundary: The minimum is over the declared evaluated FP64 component scores. It is not an exact-real optimum, a bit-identical optimization of historical np.einsum reassociations, a tree-realizability result, another dictionary's bound or a native-consumer optimum.
mathAssessment.feasibleCurrentRoute: Actual finite current-state reconstruction and its label pair are retained among the choices; component-score nonworsening is an instrument identity. Individual endpoint/response terms, rows or strata may worsen at the joint optimum.
mathAssessment.scalarPublisher: Published component norms remain producer measurements. The publisher independently reconstructs every multiply/add score from those scalar norms, checks canonical minima/ties/gaps and selected labels, and rebuilds pooled public scalars. Strict equality is consistent with separate binary64 multiplication/addition in the producer; the inherited finite close helper is used for aggregate/measure comparisons, not as a scientific success gate.
mathAssessment.historicalReduction: Global np.einsum losses, ordinary pooled RMS/cosines and all endpoint/response strata are reported separately. They do not redefine the component argmin.
mathAssessment.terminalScope: Target-assisted H1 capacity only. No source-input resolver, target-free serving improvement, useful native QKV response, full contextual successor, encoder/denoiser/decoder closure, fresh prompt generalization or pixels is established.
